content:
Wrote a three part series here on Lean's Part monad and its underlying domain theory, and how it can be used to model potentially-diverging computations.

Part 1 is an optional section on basic domain theory and fixed points. In part 2 I introduce Lean's Part and show how it allows us to define and reason about functions which may not terminate, using the Collatz function as an example (in this case, where termination is an open conjecture). In part 3 I define an imperative language Imp with while loops, give it semantics in Part, and show how to prove correctness of a loop using Hoare logic.

Other Lean things I've written about and haven't shared here are the free monad (now in CSlib) and a general technique for verified dynamic programming
